The SSL handshake error (`CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found`) occurred because Android does not trust self-signed or private development CA certificates by default. The dev server uses a custom CA certificate (`dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`), but the application lacked a Network Security Configuration allowing it as a trust anchor in debug builds.

### Changes Made

1. **Copied dev CA certificate to resources**: Added [`shelftap_dev_ca.pem`](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r3/work/app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem) under `app/src/main/res/raw/` so it is accessible via `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca`.
2. **Created Network Security Configuration**: Created [`network_security_config.xml`](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r3/work/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml) under `app/src/main/res/xml/` with `<debug-overrides>` referencing `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca`. This trusts the dev certificate during debug builds while keeping release builds secure against untrusted certificates.
3. **Registered config in manifest**: Added `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"` to the `<application>` tag in [`AndroidManifest.xml`](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r3/work/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L8).
